punchline: Playing it safe feels responsible, but it's the surest way to be ignored.
thirty_sec: Seth Godin was driving through France with his family when they fell in love with the picture-book cows along the road. Twenty minutes later, nobody was looking at them. The cows hadn't changed; they'd just become familiar. A purple cow, Godin says, would have made them stop the car. That's his case against 'very good': it's so common it's invisible. The remarkable part has to be built into the work itself.
question: What's one thing about your work that someone would actually bother mentioning to a friend?
